review_notes: I read the whole file. It has four short theorems, and each proof is a direct application of an existing lemma. `jointDickmanLaw_of_published` applies `jointDickmanLaw_of_rational_fixedScale` to `rationalFixedScaleLaw_of_published`. The two order-law theorems apply the matching `_of_jointDickmanLaw` lemma. `main_results_of_published` packages the three previous theorems in an anonymous constructor. There is no redundant intermediate step, case split or tactic block to remove. The only repeated text is the long hypothesis list `hMR hMRT hKMT hFord hSD hSW hM hMP hMV hMC hBill`. I considered shortening it with `..` or by making the hypotheses implicit. Neither is a clear improvement, because these are explicit hypotheses and can't be recovered by unification. Hiding them would also make the dependence on the published inputs harder to see, which is the point of this file. I did not inspect the imported lemmas in depth, because the proofs have nothing to simplify.
